title: Pure merit-order clearing with exact equal-price split, Decimal quantities, validated demand series
purpose: Replace marketClearing/priceGroupCalculation with a pure, exact, non-recursive clearing function. Store fractional accepted quantities as Decimal. Validate demand data before a run starts and index it by periodNumber - 1.

modify: abmem/models/models.py (Offer.acceptanceAmount, Period.metDemand, Offer.to_dict returns str for acceptanceAmount)

public_interfaces.description: Input bid. key identifies the offer (index in the offers list).

public_interfaces.signature:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClearingResult:
    accepted: Mapping[Hashable, Decimal]
    ptf: Decimal | None
    met_demand: Decimal
    offered_volume: Decimal
    marginal_group: tuple[Hashable, ...]
public_interfaces.description: accepted has an entry for every bid (Decimal 0 for rejected). ptf is the price of the highest accepted price group, None if nothing is accepted. offered_volume keeps the current semantics of Period.marketVolume (sum of offered quantities).

public_interfaces.signature: def clear_market(bids: Sequence[Bid], demand: Decimal, quantum: Decimal = Decimal('0.001')) -> ClearingResult
public_interfaces.description: Uniform-price merit order. Groups bids by equal price, ascending. A group whose total quantity fits the remaining demand D_rem is fully accepted. The first group whose total exceeds D_rem is split by equal share capped at bid quantity (water-filling, OQ-18) and the loop stops. Allocations are quantised to 'quantum' with the largest-remainder method so that their sum equals D_rem exactly. Pure, no ORM, no recursion.

public_interfaces.signature: def acceptance_prices(result: ClearingResult, bids: Sequence[Bid], strategy: MarketStrategy) -> dict[Hashable, Decimal | None]
public_interfaces.description: PAYASBID: bid price for accepted bids. PAYASPTF: result.ptf for accepted bids. None for rejected bids.

values holds the leading block of valid rows of the demand column (A8: 8808 valid rows of 43848). at(t) returns values[t - 1] for t in [1, len(values)]. validate_horizon raises DemandDataError if period_count > len(values) or if any of the first period_count values is NaN, infinite or negative , and zero values are rejected as well (OQ-12).
Message names the file, column, requested horizon and the first offending row.

invariants: Every bid with price < ptf is fully accepted. Every bid with price > ptf is rejected.
The result does not depend on the order of the input bids (permutation invariance).
Demand index: the Period with periodNumber t uses DemandSeries.at(t) == values[t-1].
edge_cases: Empty bid list: accepted = {}, ptf None, met_demand 0.
demand == 0: clear_market stays total and returns nothing accepted, ptf None. Zero demand never reaches it in a run because DemandSeries.validate_horizon rejects it (OQ-12).
Supply shortfall (offered_volume < demand): all accepted, ptf = highest bid price, met_demand = offered_volume.
Single bid larger than demand: accepted = demand, ptf = its price.
Bid with quantity 0: accepted 0 and ignored when determining ptf.
Negative, NaN or infinite price or quantity: ValueError (offers are validated earlier, so this signals a programming error).
Quantisation residual: largest remainder assigns the remaining quanta to bids with the largest fractional parts, ties broken by ascending key for determinism.
periodNumber 0 or > len(values): DemandSeries.at raises IndexError with a clear message.

resolved_open_questions.OQ-12: Zero demand is rejected by DemandSeries.validate_horizon (DemandDataError).
resolved_open_questions.OQ-18: Equal-price split = equal share capped at offer quantity (water-filling): remaining demand is split equally among tied offers, an offer whose share exceeds its quantity is capped and the surplus is re-split among the uncapped offers until demand or tied capacity is exhausted. Oracle: tied A=100, B=10, remaining D=60 gives B=10, A=50.

resolved_items.item: Equal-price split rule and the B4 test oracle
resolved_items.reason: PLAN 1.7 describes a split proportional to bid quantities. For the B4 example (A=100, B=10, D_rem=60) that rule gives A=54.545, B=5.455. The validation example in PLAN 1.7 and analiz.md B4 expects B=10, A=50, which is an equal-share split with quantity caps (each bid receives D_rem/n, a capped bid keeps its full quantity and the rest is redistributed among the others). Both are exact and single-pass. The worker implements the split only after the user confirms which rule is meant (ARCHITECTURE.md OQ-18).
resolved_items.resolution: Equal-price split = equal share capped at offer quantity (water-filling): remaining demand is split equally among tied offers, an offer whose share exceeds its quantity is capped and the surplus is re-split among the uncapped offers until demand or tied capacity is exhausted. Oracle: tied A=100, B=10, remaining D=60 gives B=10, A=50.
